items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1989-08-13
items.q: So, I had, I had met Louis before... that was the first time I met Louis. Second time I met him was about three years later.

ctx.x: And it was a black theater and I used to come out of, out of class and go across the street to the theater all the time, because I knew a lot of the musicians that were, that were playing in the, in the show. And it was during the time when I had first started doing jazz concerts. So it was 1936 and I went backstage, because his band was playing there. And I knew Louis Russell and Red Allen and people that were playing there, Al Nicholas. So, I had, I had met Louis before, I don't actually remember when, but…
Okay, we're on the second reel. Al Rose, same date. August 13th, 1989. Okay, we left off with Eus... Eus Panassia.

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: INTERVIEWER mentions 'Louis Russell orchestra' in the context of Louis Armstrong's recordings; INTERVIEWEE does not mention Louis Russell or claim any personal interaction.

ctx.x: I suppose I would agree with that, although, as a matter of fact, I never really thought that much about solos. As I mentioned to you earlier, not in this interview, but my own approach to most things is really very narrow. And for my ear, in listening to jazz, a solo is mainly an intermission. And it is very difficult for me to even pay attention to what a soloist is doing, because I am listening for the band. Now, that's a peculiarity of my own musical tastes and interest, and is not one which I particularly…

It would be fair to say that due to economic, social, political circumstances, that jazz went through various changes in forms from, let's say, what I'm familiarly, what I primarily call traditional jazz or New Orleans jazz, went through changes to, let's say, in the mid-30s swing, and then up through bebop or bop style, and then the so-called progressive jazz, all these different styles, due to various changes in the social structure. For instance, let me just give you one example. Would it be fair to say that…
Let me comment in general. Okay. Just comment in general on that kind of a scheme.
